name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (adult)
theme: the split the aml run opened

meta.title: APL in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults; newly diagnosed (Sanz low/intermediate and high risk) and the rare relapsed setting. Split from the aml row per the granularity rule: the arm family (ATRA/arsenic, largely chemo-free), the emergency (coagulopathy), and the risk system (Sanz WBC) are all different.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for APL - oncology's rescue story: once the deadliest leukemia, now the most curable, PROVIDED the first 72 hours go right. The trainer's first lesson is a co-intervention, not an arm: ATRA starts on morphologic suspicion, before genetic confirmation, because early hemorrhagic death is the disease's one remaining killer. Frontline is chemo-free ATRA-arsenic for low/intermediate risk (APL0406: 50-month OS 99.2%); the QT-prolonged heart is the main reason to fall back to ATRA-chemotherapy. Scope boundaries: pediatric APL is trial-level only here; therapy-rel…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022): APL with PML::RARA; Sanz risk (WBC <=10k low/intermediate, >10k high)
meta.response: morphologic CR + molecular remission by PML::RARA RT-qPCR

stages.label: Suspicion & stabilization
stages.question: Could this be APL - and has ATRA started YET?
stages.decision: Start ATRA on morphologic suspicion; manage coagulopathy aggressively; do not wait for genetics.

stages.label: Confirmation & risk
stages.question: Is PML::RARA confirmed, and which Sanz risk group?
stages.decision: Confirm the fusion (PCR/FISH); assign Sanz risk by presenting WBC.

stages.label: Frontline plan
stages.question: Chemo-free arsenic, or the chemotherapy fallback?
stages.decision: ATRA-ATO for low/intermediate risk; add gemtuzumab or move to ATRA-chemo for high risk; ATRA-chemo when the heart says no to arsenic.

stages.label: Molecular monitoring
stages.question: Is PML::RARA gone - and staying gone?
stages.decision: RT-qPCR at end of consolidation; molecular relapse is treated as relapse.

stages.label: Consolidation at relapse
stages.question: After salvage: autologous, allogeneic, or neither?
stages.decision: Molecular CR2 favors autologous HSCT; persistent PCR positivity points allogeneic.

stages.label: Relapse (rare)
stages.question: It came back - which salvage, given what was used before?
stages.decision: ATO-based re-induction if arsenic-naive; alternatives and trials if arsenic-exposed.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which studies fit - including the oral-arsenic future?

stages.label: Data artifacts
stages.question: Which result moves the plan most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live VOI flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: APL0406 enrolled 18-71; age carries a modest modifier, never a gate - the chemo-free regimen is exactly what makes older APL curable.
Patient.helpPatient: Age matters less here than in almost any other leukemia.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: A modifier only - APL at presentation makes everyone look sicker than their disease trajectory.
Patient.helpPatient: How unwell right now - which in this disease often improves fast once treatment starts.

Emergency.label: Coagulopathy status
Emergency.help: The disease's one remaining killer. Active bleeding applies an early-death modifier and drives the blood-product co-intervention intensity.
Emergency.helpPatient: The bleeding risk of the first days - the team's whole early focus.

Diagnostic gates.label: PML::RARA confirmation
Diagnostic gates.help: The diagnosis. Not-detected reroutes back to the AML trainer (the mirror of its APL gate). Pending withholds ranking - but ATRA-on-suspicion is already a co-intervention.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: The gene test that confirms this specific leukemia - treatment starts before it returns.

Diagnostic gates.label: Presenting WBC (Sanz risk)
Diagnostic gates.help: The whole Sanz risk system: >10k is high risk, which adds gemtuzumab to the arsenic backbone (AML17 practice) and raises early-death and relapse risk.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: The white-cell count at diagnosis - the one number that changes the plan's intensity.

Diagnostic gates.label: QT status
Diagnostic gates.help: Arsenic prolongs QT; a significantly prolonged baseline interval (or uncorrectable electrolytes) gates the ATO arms and falls back to ATRA-chemotherapy - the one common reason the chemo-free road clo…
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: A heart-rhythm check - if it flags, there is a proven chemotherapy version of the cure.

On treatment.label: PML::RARA PCR (post-consolidation)
On treatment.help: Molecular remission is the endpoint; a CONFIRMED positive after consolidation is treated as relapse before blasts return. It also picks the transplant type at relapse (negative -> autologous; positiv…
On treatment.helpPatient: The ultra-sensitive test for any trace of the leukemia gene.

On treatment.label: Prior arsenic exposure
On treatment.help: Routes the rare relapse: arsenic-naive relapse gets ATO re-induction; arsenic-exposed relapse points to alternatives and trials.
On treatment.helpPatient: Whether arsenic was part of the first treatment.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: ATRA + arsenic trioxide, chemo-free (low/intermediate risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ELN 2019 + NCCN v5.2026 standard for low/intermediate risk
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: differentiation syndrome, QT prolongation, transient hepatotoxicity - and famously little else
Newly diagnosed.patient: The chemo-free cure: a vitamin-A derivative plus arsenic infusions - the trial's survival curve is one of the best in all of cancer medicine.

Newly diagnosed.name: ATRA + arsenic + gemtuzumab (high risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: AML17-style; ELN 2019 high-risk options include GO or chemo-added regimens
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds GO hepatotoxicity to the arsenic profile; leukocytosis management
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same arsenic backbone with one antibody-drug dose added for the high-count form.

Newly diagnosed.name: ATRA + chemotherapy (AIDA-style fallback)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: ELN 2019 alternative; the arm QT-prolonged patients rank first
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: full anthracycline profile: cytopenias, alopecia, cardiotoxicity monitoring, maintenance years
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven chemotherapy version of the cure - used when the heart rhythm rules arsenic out.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always modeled; in APL the honest contrast is absolute
Newly diagnosed.patient: Always shown honestly: this is the leukemia where declining treatment and being cured are days apart on the same calendar.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: ATO-based re-induction (arsenic-naive relapse)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: ELN 2019 first choice for arsenic-naive relapse
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If arsenic was not part of round one, it is the strongest card for round two.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Autologous transplant (molecular CR2)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: ELN 2019: preferred consolidation in molecular CR2
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: transplant conditioning without GVHD - own cells returned
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Once the gene test is clean again, banking and returning your own cells consolidates the second remission.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Allogeneic transplant (persistent PCR positivity)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: treatment-related mortality and GVHD - disclosed verbatim beside benefit per honesty constraint
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the rare disease that will not clear on the gene test, a donor's marrow - with its real risks stated plainly.

milestones.title: ATRA on suspicion + coagulopathy control
review: ATRA ON SUSPICION - before genetic confirmation (ELN 2019); the diagnosis is an emergency phone call, not a scheduled consult
coagulopathy control hour-one: fibrinogen/platelet support, NO lumbar puncture/central lines until controlled
Sanz WBC gate (<=10 vs >10) picks chemo-free ATRA-ATO vs the cytoreduction add-on
differentiation-syndrome vigilance (steroids at first sign) + QTc discipline through ATO
PML::RARA PCR is the response clock - molecular relapse is treated as relapse

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' is in the manifest staleness list.
ATRA-on-suspicion renders as a permanent banner, never a rankable choice - delay is the one error this trainer exists to prevent.
The not-detected PML::RARA result reroutes to the AML trainer: the two specs hand patients to each other across one test, in both directions.
The ATRA-chemotherapy fallback renders as a cure with a harder road, never as a failure - 92.6% at 50 months is stated with the same respect as 99.2%.
Relapse-arm evidence is thin BECAUSE the frontline cure works (relapse 1.9%); the relapse screen says so in a banner rather than dressing registry estimates as trial results.
Transplant cards disclose treatment-related mortality beside benefit - and transplant renders only in the relapse setting, never frontline.
The display ceiling is 97 in 100 even where the trial reports 99.2% - certainty is never promised.
Comfort care remains modeled, with the honest note that untreated APL is fatal in days to weeks while the cure exists.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: ATRA starts on morphologic suspicion - before genetic confirmation
PML::RARA must be confirmed before ranking; not-detected reroutes to the AML trainer
significant QT prolongation gates the arsenic arms
a confirmed positive post-consolidation PCR is relapse - treat before blasts return
care: ANY presenting hospital: immediate ATRA availability (ED formulary)
ATO administration with ECG/electrolyte monitoring capability
